## Current state, as the tree reports it

Slice 30 is in and green: **1073 tests, 0 failed**, all eight `ci_local.sh --with-all --with-e2e` gates clear, 15 §16.3 scenarios passing, `dev_instance.sh` bringing up virginia in 76 seconds. `docs/MENU_AND_HANDHELD_PLAN.md` names **Stage 1b** as next and **Stage 1c** as "the honest gap."

## What I found while reading, and it changes the order

Stage 1c was deferred in Slice 30 on this stated ground:

> the fifteen §16.3 scenarios all run in one default context, and giving one of them a second viewport is either a second browser context per run or a resize that every subsequent scenario inherits.

**The harness does not work that way.** `RestaurantHarness` holds one *browser*; every scenario calls `StartInstanceAsync`, which calls `browser.NewContextAsync(…)` and hands back a context of its own — and `OpenIsolatedPageAsync` already mints and tracks further contexts per call. A viewport is a context-level setting, so there is nothing to leak. The deferral was justified by a property of the harness that the harness contradicts, and the same sentence is now quoted in **S§11.12**, **F-59's ledger row**, and the plan. That is a real finding in this project's sense — a reasoned decision resting on a fact the tree falsifies — and it is F-62.

That matters for ordering. Stage 1b is ~2,400 lines of Razor rewritten with no compiler and no browser on my side; doing it before the barrier exists repeats exactly the process that produced F-59 — four copies of a paste nobody could check. **I recommend Slice 32 = Stage 1c**, then 1b converted against a gate that can actually catch the failure. Flagging it for veto, per the standing arrangement: if you want 1b first, say so and I'll do that instead.

## What Slice 32 would contain

Now I'll author the new harness file.Now the harness changes for the handheld viewport.Now the constants the scenario reads.Now verification passes on the C#.Now the specification edits.Now the changelog entry, the F-59 correction, and the F-62 row in Appendix A.## Where Slice 32 stands

The code half is written and verified. The documentation half is roughly two-thirds done. I hit the tool limit mid-way through the Appendix A edits, so this is a status report rather than the tarball — but nothing is lost, and everything below is reproducible from `dump.txt` in one pass next turn.

## Built and checked

**`Harness/HandheldReach.cs`** (new). Navigates a page, waits on `.page-head`, and reads everything in one `EvaluateAsync` round trip so the numbers all describe the same moment. Returns document scroll width against `clientWidth`, a bounding box per control, and a best-effort name for the widest offender.

**`Harness/RestaurantInstance.cs`** — `HandheldViewportWidth = 375` / `Height = 667`, a shared `ContextOptions(baseUrl, handheld)` factory, and the same option on `OpenIsolatedPageAsync`. The wide case passes `null` rather than writing 1280×720, which would be the same number in a second place — F-48's mechanism.

**`Harness/RestaurantHarness.cs`** — `handheld` parameter threaded through. I audited all fifteen call sites: every one passes either the first positional argument or named arguments, and `cancellationToken:` is always named, so inserting the parameter before it is safe.

**`EndToEndScenarios.cs`** — scenario 16, plus its fixtures.

## Three verification results worth stating

**The C# checker is sensitive, proven one regression at a time.** Breaking a `string.Create` operand into a bare literal → caught (CS1620). Deleting a closing brace → caught. Putting `await` in an interpolation hole → caught (CS4007). All four edited files plus an untouched control are clean.

**The embedded JavaScript actually ran.** `node --check` parses it, and I exercised it against a hand-built fake DOM. Two results matter: a pill 100px past the right edge *inside* an `overflow-x: auto` strip was correctly ignored, and a rogue element outside any scroller was correctly named. That false-positive guard is the whole reason this barrier was safe to write, and it is now demonstrated rather than argued.

**No browser.** `npm install playwright-core` succeeded; the Chromium download is blocked by the egress allowlist. So the layout claims rest on reading `app.css` line by line, and the workstation's run is the one that counts.

## F-62, which is why the order changed

Slice 30 deferred this barrier on the stated ground that the scenarios share one browser context. They do not — the harness holds one *browser*, and `StartInstanceAsync` mints a fresh context per instance. A viewport belongs to a context. The deferral rested on a property of the tree that the tree contradicts, and by then the sentence had been copied into S§16.4, F-59's ledger row, and the plan. That is the finding, and it is the argument for building the barrier before Stage 1b converts 2,400 more lines of Razor blind.
